deathSays.line: You wake up with dirt in your mouth and blood on your hands that isn't yours. The sky is the wrong color — not sunset-wrong, wound-wrong. Jaxon Duffy. Hvac tech. From Columbus, Ohio. That was yesterday. This is now. You have: Home key, Mother's Ring, Field suture kit, Carpenter's square, Dead Phone. That's everything you own in this world. Haven. Twelve people. The fire is lit. Last night, something walked past the treeline on two legs. Too tall. It stopped. It listened. Then it kept going. Nobody slept after that.

🔥 The fire settles. Nicolás has been quiet all evening, and now everyone knows why. "Nevermore — I put it down today." "Its shadow detaches from the branch-shadow and slides across the ground toward you — a straight black lane, growing. The bird hasn't moved. The shadow has." "It climbs, laughing in a dead voice — out of spear reach, watching." A beat of silence, then the questions come all at once. Fatima says quietly "Did it look at you? Before?" Joyce breathes "Say that again — slower." Someone at the edge of the light says what everyone's thinking: "So — what are we calling it?"

You see smoke on the horizon. The Bloodied — 5 people, 33 days in. fishing folk, by the look of it. They know 7 plants — 5 new to you. They look lean — hungry, even. Food would talk here. They've been here the whole time.

A LOT of snake. Tough, rich, faintly fishy — and it feeds the whole village for days. The fat renders beautifully. It's dead. The carcass is there on the ground — search the body if you want the meat. But you don't know this flesh. Clean it, test it cautiously, or ask someone who knows. And don't leave it long: meat rots where it lies.
